brief: Goldman's equities desk describes a broad relief rally on 17 September 2026, the day after the Fed's rate hike, as Treasury yields took a breather and oil eased on reports China asked Iran to rein in the Houthis, with Trump potentially meeting Middle East leaders as soon as the following Tuesday over a possible Saudi pipeline restart. The S&P rose 114bps to 7,637, its second-best September session, with breadth strong (292 names green) and AI/Mag7 the largest contributors. GS research (GIR) still expects an additional Fed hike in October, keeps its neutral-rate estimate at 3.25-3.5%, and now adds a March 2028 rate cut alongside prior September and December 2027 cuts. Prime brokerage data shows TMT as the most net-bought US sector over the past month, with Mag7 net allocation near a three-year high after a June low. The close above the desk's short-term CTA threshold level is expected to reduce systematic selling pressure, and the desk expects dealers to become longer gamma into further upside than downside.
